issues.reason: Names and casing makes a multi-word name one opaque symbol built from the whole capitalized run and states the cue mechanically ('a capitalized modifier belongs to the capitalized run and joins the name' — Upper Calderwick -> upper_calderwick), and 'Old' is an adjective, not one of the kinship/courtesy title nouns (Dr, Uncle) the surface-only carve-out enumerates, so the symbol must be old_vesh.

new_gaps: A capitalized ADJECTIVAL EPITHET on a personal name ('Old Vesh', 'Young Bill') is assigned to neither bullet explicitly: the mechanical casing rule (capitalized modifier joins the run) is illustrated only on place names, while the surface-only title carve-out enumerates kinship/courtesy title NOUNS. A licensed form would need to say whether the epithet joins the symbol (old_vesh) or stays surface-only in the Name string (vesh), since both bullets otherwise reach the same sentence.
defect_summary: Compliant form: (Name old_vesh "Old Vesh") with old_vesh also filling the possessor slot of (Possession sk_father_1 ...) — one symbol for the whole capitalized run, one Name atom, and no separate (Member ... old) atom.
notes: Nothing else is at fault: the kinship genitive takes the opaque Possession, capitalized 'a Keeper' stays a common noun with no Name atom, the copular-with-time-modifier reification (state witness + Experiencer + Past + flat Past-wrapped copular) matches the stated pattern, and 'sixty-three years ago' correctly anchors as (BeforeBy sk_keeper_1 now 63 year).
